**STEP 1 - Scene:** This is a single piece of cooked sweet corn on the cob, a cross-section cut from an ear, on a white square plate. The photo is taken from directly above, so the cut end of the cob faces the camera.

**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The plate is a square dinner-style plate, about 24 cm across. Its area is roughly 450-500 cm². The corn piece measures about 6 cm across the cut face.

**STEP 3 - Items:** One item is corn on the cob (cut segment, kernels and cob core). No oil, butter, or sauce is visible.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The corn covers about 7% of the plate (about 33 cm² of roughly 450 cm²).

**STEP 5 - Volume:** The segment is roughly a 6 cm diameter cylinder about 4 cm long. Volume is about 33 cm² × 4 cm ≈ 130 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Corn on the cob is partly dense kernel and partly lighter cob core, so I use a bulk density of about 0.55 g/ml. That gives 130 ml × 0.55 ≈ 70 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Boiled sweet corn is about 96 kcal per 100 g. So 70 g × 0.96 ≈ 67 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** A single 4 cm cob segment is a small portion, so about 70 g and roughly 65 kcal is plausible. A whole medium ear is about 100-150 g, and this piece is a fraction of that.

Total: about 70 g, about 67 kcal.
